label: thm:ftc1
title: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b = [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$. Then the function $F(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$ satisfies $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\; x)\; x$. In Mathlib the core result is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}, which requires three hypotheses: (1) $\texttt{IntervalIntegrable}\; f\; \texttt{volume}\; a\; x$, (2) $\texttt{StronglyMeasurableAtFilter}\; f\; (\texttt{nhds}\; x)\; \texttt{volume}$, and (3) $\texttt{ContinuousAt}\; f\; x$.
proof: We establish three prerequisites for \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}: (1) $\texttt{IntervalIntegrable}\; f\; \texttt{volume}\; a\; x$: since $f$ is continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b$, it is interval integrable on $[a,b]$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:continuous_interval_integrable}, and we restrict to $[a,x]$ via monotonicity of interval integrability (\texttt{IntervalIntegrable.mono\_set}); (2) $\texttt{StronglyMeasurableAtFilter}\; f\; (\texttt{nhds}\; x)\; \texttt{volume}$: by Lemma~\ref{lem:strongly_measurable_interior}, since $x$ belongs to the open interior; (3) $\texttt{ContinuousAt}\; f\; x$: by Lemma~\ref{lem:continuous_at_interior}. The result then follows directly from \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}.
